subject: RFP: Data Residency Annex & Indemnity Flowdown - redline coordination
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@medixhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medixhealth.com, MedixHealth Legal Team <legal@medixhealth.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: MedixHealth RFP - legal annex + data residency details

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Procurement and legal asked that we collect a few final clarifications before the shortlist: specifically a short annex addressing Data Residency (locations, sub‑processing), an indemnity flowdown for downstream vendors, and confirmation of liability cap calculations tied to order form spend.

Attached is our Legal Annex template (PDF) and a short spreadsheet with order form examples that the finance team will use to validate caps. Can you:
- Confirm which Redwood deployments support firm-level data residency commitments (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Provide a redline of the indemnity paragraph with suggested flowdown language for our downstream placements
- Confirm the proposed liability cap math for a three‑year order form example in the spreadsheet

Would appreciate an initial response by end of day Thursday so our procurement committee can include your answers in the vendor scoring. If easier, we can set a 30‑minute legal call on Friday.

Carlos
Procurement Manager, MedixHealth

Attachments: MedixHealth_RFP_Legal_Annex_v1.pdf, OrderForm_Example.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@medixhealth.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-12T12:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedixHealth RFP - legal annex + data residency details

Hi Carlos — thanks for sending. We can get you an initial pass today on the annex and redline. Quick notes up front:
- Deployment options: Hosted API (multi‑region) — no contractual data residency guarantees by default; Dedicated — region pinning available (EU/US) with contractual residency limits; Private — customer‑managed (VPC/on‑prem) supports firm-level residency commitments.
- Indemnity: Redwood proposes a limited IP indemnity for infringement claims tied to our model and code, with a standard liability cap tied to annual fees (suggested language attached). We do not accept unbounded downstream flowdown for customer contracts; proposing a carve with conditional flowdown tied to purchase of Dedicated/Private offerings.

I’m looping in Aditya and Dev for technical and commercial confirmation; Grace O'Connor from sales will be on the follow-up for commercial terms. Expect a redline PDF and a quick liability calc by EOD.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference

—
Neha Kapoor
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Attachments referenced: —

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: MedixHealth annex + liability math (notes)

Neha / Dev — quick internal note after looking at the annex and the spreadsheet:

1) Data residency
- Hosted: we can offer region-aware routing and customer tenancy separation but cannot contractually restrict physical data residency unless they buy Dedicated or Private.
- Dedicated: we can guarantee processing in a single region and provide SOC/audit attestations. Need to confirm runbook for cross‑region failover (we currently allow failover but can make it manual/controlled for an SLA).
- Private: covered; ops/installation schedule impacts timeline and pricing.

Action: Dev — can you confirm the failover behavior and whether we can require manual approval for cross‑region fallback? If yes, provide wording we can commit to for the annex (e.g., "No cross‑region replication without Customer written approval").

2) Indemnity flowdown
- Legal preference: limited IP indemnity plus defense for third‑party IP claims; we need to avoid open-ended indemnity for customer downstream contracts.
- Suggest offering conditional flowdown: if customer requires flowdown to a downstream entity that Redwood does not control, flowdown applies only to claims caused by Redwood's breach or Redwood‑provided deliverables; otherwise customer remains responsible to obtain flowdown from their vendors.

3) Liability cap math
- For order form example (3 years, $1.2M total): propose cap = 12 months of average recurring fees (standard), which would compute to $400k (if annualized). Provide worked example in response PDF.

Neha — once Dev confirms the failure mode text, I can draft the redline for the indemnity and run the liability calc.

-Aditya

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-13T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: MedixHealth annex + liability math (notes)

Aditya / Neha — confirm: production failover is configurable. By default our Hosted clusters have an automated cross‑region failover for resilience; however, we can implement a policy flag for "manual cross‑region failover" for Dedicated customers which requires customer approval before failing over. That is a deployment configuration and adds ~2 weeks to onboarding for Dedicated and ~1 week for Private (on‑prem).

Proposed annex wording: "Redwood will not replicate Customer data to regions outside the contracted region absent Customer written authorization or a documented emergency failover event. For Dedicated deployments, Redwood will implement a manual‑approval failover process when requested at provisioning; documented in the Service Runbook."

Also: we can provide a SOC/ISO attestation copy for Dedicated and Private when requested; we cannot provide that for the multi‑tenant hosted API beyond standard security summary.

-Dev

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@medixhealth.com>
Cc: legal@medixhealth.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-17T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MedixHealth RFP - legal annex + data residency details

Carlos / MedixTeam — attaching our response package and a redline (see attachments). Summary of deliverables in this email for quick review:

1) Data residency & failover
- For Dedicated purchases we confirm contractual region pinning and the option for "manual cross‑region failover" at provisioning. Proposed text (excerpt): "Redwood will not replicate Customer data to regions outside the contracted region absent Customer written authorization or a documented emergency failover event. For Dedicated deployments, manual‑approval failover is available and will be documented in the Service Runbook."

2) Indemnity & flowdown
- Attached is a redline of your indemnity paragraph. High level: Redwood provides an IP indemnity limited to Redwood‑owned code and model artifacts, subject to timely notice and control of defense. We propose conditional flowdown for downstream vendors: Redwood will accept flowdown liability only for claims directly caused by Redwood's breach or Redwood‑supplied deliverables. We cannot agree to unconditional, full flowdown to downstream parties.

3) Liability cap calculation
- Worked example included for the 3‑year, $1.2M order form: proposed cap = 12 months of recurring fees = $400k. Worked math in attached spreadsheet and assumptions noted.

Next steps:
- If the language is acceptable, we can prepare a final clean redline and provide DocuSign links for the order form and annex.
- If Medix requires any additional concessions (e.g., higher cap, deeper flowdown), please indicate and we can loop Legal/Revenue Ops for approval.

Available for a 30‑minute call Friday 6/20 9–11am PT if you want to walk through.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: RW_Response_Annex_redline_v2.pdf, DataResidency_Appendix_table.xlsx
